scope: Mac generation-correlated editor admission, callback, GPU wait and native preparation diagnostics; no scheduler/color policy change
changes: Existing EditSession signposts now use PointsOfInterest, which the standard Time Profiler template actually records; the previous EditSession category was absent from its export.
RenderAdmission spans the actual forwarding task through its resumed actor return; end metadata identifies the admitted generation.
FastCallback includes the whole scheduled callback, including the snapshot wait; existing fast/refine intervals also carry generations.
GpuDriverAwait encloses the actual driver call, and GpuPublished marks current-generation acknowledged submission after all existing guards.
NativeAutoPrepare covers native worker execution; BenchmarkDrag labels the opt-in benchmark arm.
No new settings, thread pool, task priority, image buffer, math, model, Rust/WGSL/ABI or XMP schema changes. Scheduling, cancellation and source ownership behavior stays the same.

method: Pair Begin/End by exact interval identifier and name; deduplicate identical exported rows.
Match published generations inside each labeled drag to their scheduler, callback and driver intervals; generation counters are scoped by the separate drag windows.
Schedule start excludes preceding model observer work and gesture dispatch; publication is the actual current GPU acknowledgement event, not monitor observation or scanout.
RenderAdmission ends on forwarding-task resumption. A callback can already be running before that return: this interval alone cannot isolate actor queue delay.
Only successfully correlated publications get the partition; canceled/coalesced callbacks are not counted as zero-latency samples.
NativeAutoPrepare begins at worker entry and excludes prior admission queue wait.
This is one instrumented shared-host run, not performance qualification or a causal proof of Rayon starvation.

findings.meaning: In this instrumented point, late published ticks involve several boundaries. The worst 10-patch exposure schedule spends 20.386ms before the driver and 8.021ms after its return; it cannot be explained by its 2.808ms driver await alone.
findings.scopeOfMaximum: Worst correlated published generation inside the labeled drags only, excluding cold opens and unacknowledged/canceled requests.
findings.caution: The larger all-interval maxima include cold or unacknowledged/canceled work and must not be substituted for published-input latency. Do not sum maxima from different generations.
findings.forwarderOrdering: All correlated callbacks begin after forwarding return in this point; that is observed ordering, not a guaranteed contract. RenderAdmission alone does not isolate actor queue wait.
findings.next: Inspect and correlate source/generation awaits inside the pre-driver and post-driver regions during pending native preparation before changing admission or worker policy.
